destination.title: Moduli dynamics, stabilization and compactification tests
destination.question: How do source-specific compactifications generate and control moduli dynamics, and what stabilization, vacuum, particle-physics, cosmological and geometric questions arise?
destination.summary: Organize by scientific target and method across numerical batches. Preserve correction calculations, consistency tests and neighboring geometric questions as useful directions without requiring every source to construct a stabilized vacuum.

systems: Source-specified geometric and non-geometric type IIB compactifications and F-theory settings
Supplied type IIA, M-theory, heterotic and orbifold effective models
Lower-dimensional and five-dimensional settings retained with their own field content
targets: Moduli potentials, stabilization and remaining mobile directions
Corrected geometry, effective couplings and approximation control
Vacuum energy, local stability, distributions and searches
Global realization, supersymmetry breaking and physical scales
Inflation, reheating, early dark energy and late-time dynamics
Neighboring tensor, singularity and transition questions through comparison routes
regimes: Distinct flux, perturbative, nonperturbative and mixed constructions
Large-volume, weak-coupling, finite-modulus and order-one-modulus regimes where specified
Static vacua, partially stabilized systems and evolving cosmological fields
Different effective dimensions and cosmological epochs kept explicit
assumptions: Membership supplies no shared stabilization, uplift, hierarchy or control premise
Absence of a modulus differs from dynamical stabilization
Correction calculations, vacuum existence, full stability and global realization are separate targets
Child ledgers establish attributed descendant coverage; current unit rows describe only supplied contrasts

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How can an internal volume become very large while one four-cycle remains comparatively small? This example separates the growing cycle \(\tau_5\) from the smaller cycle \(\tau_4\) through a difference of their three-halves powers.

sources.title: Early Dark Energy in Type IIB String Theory

evidence.text: Can type IIB compactifications realize V=V0[1−cos(ϕ/f)]³ with phenomenological EDE parameters, controlled dS moduli stabilization, decoupled non-EDE modes and little microscopic tuning? A globally consistent Calabi–Yau embedding is a further stated goal.

sources.title: Non-perturbative stabilization of two Kähler moduli in type-IIB/F theory and the inflaton potential

evidence.text: Does extending nonperturbative stabilization from one to two Kähler moduli, together with perturbative Kähler corrections and D-term uplift, produce slow-roll plateau potentials and viable inflationary parameters?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Does the conjectured KK correction spoil stabilization and the gaugino hierarchy in the explicit two-modulus large-volume model?

sources.title: String Landscape and the Standard Model of Particle Physics

evidence.text: How can fluxes stabilize compactification parameters when the displayed superpotential omits Kähler moduli?

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which combinations of quantum corrections and additional sources can stabilize Kähler moduli while preserving a controlled large-volume expansion? The appendix compares mechanisms by their competing potential terms, flux-superpotential magnitude, topology, and gauge-sector assumptions.

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which cycle can support the nonperturbative contribution used to stabilize a small modulus inside a much larger compactification? The source selects a rigid blow-up cycle resolving a point-like singularity and distinguishes this requirement from the unfluxed instanton eligibility statement.

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How do quantum corrections lift the tree-level Kähler-modulus flat directions of type IIB flux compactifications? The effective description separates flux-sensitive axio-dilaton and complex-structure fields from cycle-volume moduli whose perturbative dynamics arise through the Kähler potential.

sources.title: Type IIA/M-theory Moduli fixing in a Class of Orientifold Models

evidence.text: How does a complex constant superpotential contribution enable moduli stabilization in a class of Type IIA orientifolds and their M-theory duals, and how do consistency restrictions and vacuum distributions depend on the chosen Kähler potential?

sources.title: Axion Stabilization in Type IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Can B2 and C2 axions in type IIB orientifolds with h1,1− ≠ 0 be stabilized within extensions of KKLT/LVS, and how do their corrections affect volume stabilization?

sources.title: String Loop Moduli Stabilisation and Cosmology in IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Under what geometric and perturbative conditions can type IIB LARGE Volume Scenarios stabilize Kähler moduli, and what inflationary and finite-temperature cosmology follows?

sources.title: Kähler moduli inflation and WMAP7

evidence.text: Do effective single-field Kähler-moduli inflation potentials from explicit type-IIB large-volume compactifications produce sufficient e-folding, a suitable scalar spectral index and suitable running relative to the historical WMAP7 ranges? A simpler exponential toy potential is also analyzed.

sources.title: Sequestering in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Does sequestering by geometric separation or strong warping survive nonperturbative stabilization of Kähler moduli, and what soft terms follow in KKLT and Large Volume Scenario compactifications?

sources.title: Poly-instanton Inflation

evidence.text: Can poly-instanton effects generate viable single-field inflation from a fibre Kähler modulus while the total volume remains stabilized and perturbative corrections remain small enough to avoid the η-problem?

sources.title: D-Branes at del Pezzo Singularities: Global Embedding and Moduli Stabilisation

evidence.text: Can phenomenologically interesting fractional-D3 quivers at del Pezzo singularities be embedded in compact type IIB orientifolds while satisfying global consistency conditions and stabilising the Kähler moduli?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization and Inflationary Cosmology with Poly-Instantons in Type IIB Orientifolds

evidence.text: Can poly-instanton corrections stabilize a Wilson-line divisor's Kähler modulus in a controlled LARGE volume model and generate viable slow-roll inflation when that modulus is displaced?

sources.title: Building an explicit de Sitter

evidence.text: Can a global type IIB construction realize Kähler uplifting with explicit branes and fluxes, geometric moduli stabilized in metastable de Sitter, and sufficiently large condensing gauge groups for volume control?

sources.title: Accidental inflation from Kähler uplifting

evidence.text: Can single-Kähler-modulus inflation in the Kähler uplifting scenario support slow roll followed by a nearby metastable dS vacuum, including the quantum corrections considered in this paper?

sources.title: Explicit de Sitter Flux Vacua for Global String Models with Chiral Matter

evidence.text: Can explicit flux stabilization of the dilaton and complex structure be combined with Kähler stabilization admitting de Sitter minima in a globally consistent type IIB compactification with chiral matter?

sources.title: Towards the core of the cosmological constant problem

evidence.text: Can a proposed Type IIB self-tuning mechanism cancel the cosmological constant despite nonzero moduli and brane vacuum energies, using a negative-potential KKLT minimum as the present background?

sources.title: Challenges for Large-Field Inflation and Moduli Stabilization

evidence.text: Can supersymmetry-breaking Kähler-moduli stabilization support large-field chaotic inflation without a stabilizer, and how do backreaction and vacuum stability constrain its potential and observables?

sources.title: Accidental Kähler moduli inflation

evidence.text: Can racetrack tuning produce prolonged inflation near an inflection point of a small Kähler modulus while stabilizing the other moduli, reducing sensitivity to string-loop corrections and relaxing the required gauge-rank hierarchy?

sources.title: Starobinsky-Type Inflation from $\alpha'$-Corrections

evidence.text: Can higher-derivative α′³ corrections generate a controlled, finite-width Starobinsky-type inflationary plateau for a Kähler modulus, with string loops supplying stabilization and a graceful exit?

sources.title: Aspects of moduli stabilization in type IIB string theory

evidence.text: How do KKLT and LVS stabilize type IIB moduli, and what consequences follow for supersymmetry breaking, low-energy phenomenology, inflation, destabilization and moduli backreaction?

sources.title: A new class of de Sitter vacua in String Theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Can the complex-structure sector remain stable after quantum corrections in large-volume type IIB vacua whose volume is only moderately large, especially when the number of moduli exceeds O(100)? Can stability arise without making this sector much heavier than the gravitino?

sources.title: String Moduli Stabilization at the Conifold

evidence.text: Can flux stabilization near a conifold generate controllable exponential mass hierarchies without significant warping, combine with large-volume Kähler stabilization, and support an aligned axion inflation model?

sources.title: The Swampland Conjecture and F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Can KKLT stabilization retain a heavy Kähler modulus while a quantized open-string coupling generates a sufficiently light inflaton and a large backreaction threshold?

sources.title: Challenges for Moduli Stabilization and String Cosmology near the Conifold

evidence.text: Can flux stabilisation near a conifold support a controlled effective theory and periodic, KNP-like aligned large-field inflation once warping, Kähler stabilisation, higher period corrections and mass hierarchies are included?

sources.title: Global Orientifolded Quivers with Inflation

evidence.text: Can an orientifolded chiral quiver at a singularity be embedded in a compact type-IIB model satisfying global brane constraints, with stabilized closed-string moduli, a tunable Minkowski/de Sitter vacuum and viable inflation in the same geometry?

sources.title: On D-brane dynamics and moduli stabilization

evidence.text: How do forces among pinned fractional branes, antibranes and orientifold planes modify Kähler-modulus potentials, and under what conditional circumstances do they assist or obstruct stabilization? The stated aim is qualitative illustration through a toy model, rather than a realistic stabilized compactification.

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: The proposed diagnostic compares a candidate DBI-induced tension with a corresponding Chern–Simons charge term under BPS assumptions. Applying it to the listed flux–curvature terms remains heuristic.

sources.title: String Landscape and the Standard Model of Particle Physics

evidence.text: Compute the specified bundle indices, set the five Standard Model multiplicities to a common generation number, and impose vanishing indices for the displayed unwanted sectors.

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Estimate the surviving Coleman–Weinberg powers using a gravitino mass and a sector cutoff, then compare them with the corrected Kähler potential. The procedure tests parametric consistency and must be accompanied by an effective-theory hierarchy check.

sources.title: Type IIA/M-theory Moduli fixing in a Class of Orientifold Models

evidence.text: Construct the four-dimensional N = 1 F-term potential V = e^K(g^{I J̄}D_IW D_J̄W̄ − 3|W|²). Use homogeneity identities, eliminate the axion-dependent W1 combination, and solve supersymmetry equations and polynomial branches of ∂_I V = 0.

sources.title: Axion Stabilization in Type IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Analytic inversion of the Kähler metric on the dilaton/Kähler/axion sector using index-based ansätze, followed by evaluation of the N=1 F-term potential. Minimization is performed in real scalar coordinates, where the volume depends only on geometric two-cycle moduli.

sources.title: String Loop Moduli Stabilisation and Cosmology in IIB Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Uses low-energy loop scaling and the Coleman–Weinberg potential to motivate corrections and cancellations; expresses the one-loop scalar potential through the tree-level Kähler metric and conjectured Kähler-potential correction.

sources.title: Runaway in the Landscape

evidence.text: This construction removes Kähler moduli so that a type IIB flux superpotential can involve every surviving geometric modulus and the axio-dilaton. It supplies a setting in which flux stabilization can be studied without adding the usual Kähler-modulus superpotential terms.

sources.title: Stabilising all Kähler moduli in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Can perturbative α′, string-loop and higher-derivative corrections stabilize the overall volume and remaining Kähler size moduli at exponentially large volume, and can additional uplift terms produce de Sitter minima?

destination.title: Anomalies, consistency and six-dimensional theory structure
destination.question: How do anomaly and related consistency tests constrain specified field theories, and how do spectra, symmetry, geometry, limits and reductions organize six-dimensional theories and their realizations?
destination.summary: The supplied contrasts support anomaly cancellation, stronger consistency tests and methodological boundary questions. Attributed child scopes support additional construction, symmetry, dynamics and limit questions. Existing scoped questions provide navigation across batches; the numerical batches remain provenance.

systems: Chiral gauge theories, supergravity and ordinary quantum field theories
String compactifications, branes, charged strings and topological phases
Six-dimensional SCFTs, gravity theories and string vacua
targets: Global gauge structure, admissible backgrounds and charge data
String-probe, lattice and Coulomb-branch consistency tests
Spectra, bounds, geometric realizations and construction obstructions
Symmetries, defects, phases, weak-coupling limits and dimensional reduction
regimes: Dimension, supersymmetry, tensor content and matter content remain source-specific
Gauge sectors and complete gravitational theories remain distinct
Gravity coupling, gravity decoupling and branch limits remain distinct
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work remains eligible

conventions: Gauge algebra, global gauge group and combined spacetime/internal structure are distinct data

sources.title: An Analysis of Anomaly Cancellation for Theories in D=10

evidence.text: Can low rank evade an exclusion based only on a nominal sixth-order defining trace?

sources.title: 8d gauge anomalies and the topological Green-Schwarz mechanism

evidence.text: Which eight-dimensional N=1 gauge theories have global gauge anomalies, and which anomalies can be canceled by coupling to topological degrees of freedom? The motivating cases are odd orthogonal groups, F4, G2 and the string-realized Sp(N) theories.

sources.title: The Global Anomaly of the Self-Dual Field in General Backgrounds

evidence.text: How do flat background Wilson lines and torsion fluxes modify the self-dual field’s global anomaly, and how do anomaly holonomies determine its physical theta characteristic?

sources.title: On the Classification of 6D SCFTs and Generalized ADE Orbifolds

evidence.text: Which minimal six-dimensional SCFTs arise from F-theory, which quotient singularities can occur as their endpoint bases, and how can additional E-string sectors and gauge-algebra tunings generate non-minimal theories?

sources.title: An Analysis of Anomaly Cancellation for Theories in D=10

evidence.text: Does the familiar quartet exhaust the specified ten-dimensional local anomaly test, including products containing low-rank simple factors?

sources.title: Line Operators in the Standard Model

evidence.text: How do the genuine electric, magnetic and dyonic line operators, theta-angle identifications and electromagnetic charges depend on the Standard Model's global gauge group G = [U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3)]/Γ, with Γ = 1, Z2, Z3 or Z6?

sources.title: Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs

evidence.text: Does classifying geometric F-theory tensor branches exhaust six-dimensional SCFTs? Known string constructions and homomorphism matches support this possibility, while frozen phases and potential interacting tensorless theories leave gaps.

sources.title: Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs

evidence.text: Do anomaly cancellation and negative-definite tensor pairing imply an interacting fixed point? Two explicit gauge candidates remain unresolved here, while a vector-free isolated tensor is reported apparently inconsistent.

sources.title: Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs

evidence.text: How do string/M/F-theory constructions organize six-dimensional SCFTs, constrain their classification beyond anomaly cancellation, and permit calculations of anomalies, RG flows and protected state counts?

sources.title: Dai-Freed anomalies in particle physics

evidence.text: Does requiring an unambiguous fermion partition-function phase on arbitrary allowed manifolds and gauge bundles impose constraints beyond traditional local and global anomalies, particularly for the Standard Model, GUTs and discrete symmetries?

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: What replaces a six-dimensional gauge theory as its gauge coupling vanishes at fixed gravitational strength? The paper studies wrapped D3-brane strings and their charged excitations along this Kähler-moduli limit.

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a six-dimensional brane gauge coupling vanish while the Planck mass remains finite? The investigation asks how compactification geometry and additional light degrees of freedom obstruct the apparent continuous global symmetry.

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Must singlet charges set the normalization of all massless abelian charges in the presence of nonabelian factors?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which matter representations occupy the largest-dimensional branches of six-dimensional supergravity for a specified gauge group?

sources.title: Emergent strings, duality and weak coupling limits for two-form fields

evidence.text: What replaces a gravitational effective description when a two-form gauge field becomes weakly coupled at infinite distance? The analyzed examples are six-dimensional F-theory and Type IIB compactifications with different supersymmetry.

sources.title: Branes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a family with arbitrarily many tensors and E8 gauge factors pass the string-probe test for a specified anomaly-lattice realization?

sources.title: Branes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can string unitarity exclude anomaly-allowed SU(N) theories with symmetric matter even though the source reports no F-theory realization?

sources.title: Branes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Does the anomaly-free SU(N) × SU(N) family permit arbitrarily large N once the consistency of its charged strings is imposed?

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: How much of the global SM gauge group is fixed by its known matter representations? The supplied representations permit four central quotients, although the global groups can differ in their nonperturbative observables and anomalies.

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: How does the Pati–Salam classification depend on taking an additional internal central quotient before identifying spacetime fermion parity?

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: Which combined spacetime and internal symmetry structure should constrain anomalies? Identifying fermion parity with an internal central element changes the admissible backgrounds and can change the anomaly classification.

sources.title: Beyond Standard Models and Grand Unifications: Anomalies, Topological Terms, and Dynamical Constraints via Cobordisms

evidence.text: What changes in the Pati–Salam classification when the spacetime/internal fermion-parity quotient is taken without the additional internal quotient of Section 4.1?

sources.title: Four-dimensional $\mathbf{\mathcal{N}=4}$ SYM theory and the swampland

evidence.text: Which discrete ranks and actual gauge groups are allowed beyond the continuous rank ceiling? The paper also asks whether analogous massless-mode bounds hold with eight supercharges in dimensions six and below.

sources.title: Swampland Constraints on 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity

evidence.text: The application seeks a required magnetic probe in a U(1)×G theory. Positive coupling coefficients and instanton masses motivate choosing the positive unit U(1) string, after perturbative charged thresholds have been absorbed.

sources.title: Implications of the weak gravity conjecture in anomalous quiver gauge theories

evidence.text: Can anomaly cancellation make surviving gauge repulsion too weak to satisfy conjectured gravitational and scalar-force bounds when a chiral theory contains many abelian gauge factors?

sources.title: Implications of the weak gravity conjecture in anomalous quiver gauge theories

evidence.text: The cycle is a tractable family in which matter determines anomaly constraints and the number of original gauge factors can vary.

sources.title: Cobordism Conjecture, Anomalies, and the String Lamppost Principle

evidence.text: Can cobordism triviality and lower-dimensional anomaly cancellation explain gaps in gauge-group ranks, constrain global gauge forms, and support the String Lamppost Principle for theories with sixteen supercharges?

sources.title: Lectures on the Swampland Program in String Compactifications

evidence.text: How can the gauge coupling vanish without decompactifying the six-dimensional theory?

sources.title: Effective field theory of 6D SUSY RG Flows

evidence.text: How does the dilaton–axion effective action constrain six-dimensional RG flows when conformal and continuous global symmetries break together, particularly on tensor, Higgs and mixed branches of SCFTs?

sources.title: Exploring the landscape of CHL strings on T$^{d}$

evidence.text: Which non-Abelian gauge groups of maximal left-moving rank d+8 occur in the CHL branch, at which moduli, and with what global topology? The systematic classification concentrates on d=1,2.

sources.title: The Global Anomaly of the Self-Dual Field in General Backgrounds
